column1: indistinct§The signature is indistinct on every copy, and the original has been missing since the fire in 1954.§每一份副本上的签名都**模糊不清**，而原件自 1954 年那场火灾后就下落不明。§in-（不）+ distinct（清晰的）
individuality§The school prizes individuality in its brochure and grades it out of existence in its classrooms.§这所学校在宣传册上珍视**个性**，在课堂上却用评分把它抹平。§
indivisible§The estate was indivisible under the old will, which is why four heirs shared one house for thirty years.§按旧遗嘱这份产业**不可分割**，所以四位继承人共用一栋房子三十年。§in-（不）+ divis（分开，同 divide 分割）

indolence§His indolence was legendary in the department and entirely confined to work that he personally considered pointless.§他的**懒散**在系里远近闻名，而且完全只针对他本人认为毫无意义的工作。§in-（不）+ dol（痛，同 condolence 吊唁）→ 不肯吃苦
indomitable§The indomitable old woman fought the compulsory purchase for eleven years and, at ninety-one, won.§这位**不屈不挠的**老太太与强制征收抗争十一年，在九十一岁时赢了。§in-（不）+ domit（驯服，同 dominate 支配）
inducement§The inducement was not money but a title, and it worked on precisely the person it was designed for.§这个**诱因**不是钱而是一个头衔，而它恰好对它所针对的那个人管用。§in-（进入）+ duc（引导，同 conduct 引导）
induction§Induction from four cases produced a rule that the fifth case demolished within a month.§从四个案例做出的**归纳**得出一条规则，第五个案例一个月内就推翻了它。§in-（进入）+ duct（引导）→ 由个别引出一般
indulge§She indulged the committee's questions for an hour and then answered the one nobody had asked.§她**耐着性子应付**了委员会一小时的提问，然后回答了那个没人问过的问题。§in-（进入）+ dulg（放任）
indulgence§The indulgence shown to one department created a grievance in the other four that lasted a decade.§对某个部门的**纵容**在另外四个部门造成了持续十年的不满。§
indulgent§An indulgent editor let the book run to nine hundred pages, and the paperback cut two hundred of them.§一位**宽容的**编辑让这本书写到九百页，而平装本删掉了其中两百页。§
industrious§The most industrious student in the class was not the quickest, and she finished the degree first.§班上最**勤奋的**学生并非最快的那个，而她最先拿到学位。§industri（勤劳）
ineffable§The taste is ineffable in the strict sense: nine tasters described it and no two used the same words.§这种味道严格说来**难以言表**——九位品评者描述它，没有两人用了同样的词。§in-（不）+ ef-（出）+ fa（说，同 fable 寓言）
ineffectual§Four warnings proved ineffectual, and the fifth worked only because it came with a deadline.§四次警告都**无济于事**，第五次奏效只因它附带了期限。§
inefficacious§The remedy is inefficacious at the dose people can afford and effective at four times that.§这种药在人们负担得起的剂量下**无效**，在四倍剂量下才有效。§
inept§His inept handling of the announcement turned a routine change into a nine-day story.§他对这次公告**笨拙的**处理，把一项例行变动变成了持续九天的新闻。§in-（不）+ ept（合适，同 apt 恰当的）
ineptitude§The ineptitude was collective: four people checked the document and none of them read past page two.§这种**无能**是集体性的——四个人检查过这份文件，没有一个读过第二页。§
inert§The gas is inert, which is exactly why it was chosen to fill a case holding a thousand-year-old document.§这种气体是**惰性的**，这正是它被选来充填存放千年文书的展柜的原因。§in-（不）+ ert ← art（技艺／活动，同 art 技艺）→ 不起作用
inescapable§The conclusion is inescapable once you accept the two premises, and both premises are contestable.§一旦接受这两个前提，结论便**无可回避**，而两个前提都可以质疑。§
inevitability§The inevitability was manufactured: four people decided in March what everyone else discovered in September.§这种**必然性**是制造出来的——四个人三月做的决定，其余人九月才发现。§
inevitably§Costs inevitably rose once the specification changed, and nobody had budgeted for the fourth revision.§规格一改，成本**不可避免地**上涨，而没人为第四次修订编过预算。§
inexorable§The decline was inexorable and slow enough that no single year looked like the year to act.§这种衰退是**不可阻挡的**，又慢到没有哪一年看起来像该出手的那一年。§in-（不）+ exor（劝动）→ 求不动
inexplicable§The gap in the record is inexplicable, and four archivists have now looked for the missing volume.§记录中的这处空缺**无法解释**，已有四位档案员找过那册失踪的卷宗。§in-（不）+ ex-（出）+ plic（折叠，同 explain 解释）
infallible§No method is infallible, and the danger begins the moment a laboratory starts believing that one is.§没有方法是**绝无差错的**，危险始于实验室开始相信某种方法万无一失的那一刻。§in-（不）+ fall（欺骗／失误，同 fail 失败）
infamous§The infamous clause was inserted in 1978 and remained unnoticed until a journalist read the whole act.§这条**臭名昭著的**条款是 1978 年塞进去的，直到一名记者通读全法才被注意到。§in-（不）+ fam（名声，同 fame 名声）
infatuation§The infatuation lasted four months and the debt it produced took eleven years to pay off.§这段**迷恋**持续四个月，它造成的债务花了十一年才还清。§in-（进入）+ fatu（愚蠢）→ 昏了头
infelicity§A single infelicity of phrasing turned an apology into an insult and cost him the appointment.§措辞上一处**不当**把道歉变成了侮辱，让他丢了那个职位。§in-（不）+ felic（幸运／恰当，同 felicity 幸福）
inferiority§A sense of inferiority drove him to work harder than anyone and to be impossible to work with.§一种**自卑**感驱使他比谁都拼命，也让他难以共事。§infer（低，同 inferior 较差的）
infighting§Infighting inside the coalition consumed nine months, and the actual policy was written by two civil servants.§联盟内部的**内斗**耗掉九个月，而实际政策是两名公务员写的。§
inflammatory§The inflammatory paragraph was cut before broadcast and leaked, in full, the following afternoon.§那段**煽动性的**文字在播出前被删，第二天下午全文泄露。§in-（进入）+ flam（火焰，同 flame 火焰）
inflexibility§The inflexibility of the rule is its whole point, and it is also why it fails in about one case in nine.§这条规则的**僵硬**正是它的要义所在，也正是它约每九例中失灵一次的原因。§
inflexible§The schedule was inflexible and the weather was not, and four weeks of work were lost to rain.§日程是**僵化的**而天气不是，四周的工作因雨报废。§in-（不）+ flex（弯曲，同 flexible 灵活的）
informal§The informal agreement held for nine years and collapsed the week the two men who made it retired.§这项**非正式的**约定维持了九年，在达成它的两人退休那周瓦解。§
infrequent§Inspections are so infrequent here that a fault can run for two years before anyone records it.§这里的检查**如此稀少**，一处故障可以运行两年才有人记录。§
infusion§An infusion of four hundred thousand pounds kept the theatre open and bought it about eighteen months.§四十万英镑的**注入**让这家剧院得以开门，也为它买来约十八个月的时间。§in-（进入）+ fus（倒，同 confuse 混淆）
ingenue§She was cast as the ingenue at twenty-two and spent the next decade trying to be given anything else.§她二十二岁时被定型演**天真少女**，此后十年都在争取别的角色。§
ingenuous§His ingenuous account of the meeting was more damaging than any deliberate leak would have been.§他对那次会议**天真坦白的**叙述，比任何蓄意泄密都更具破坏力。§in-（在内）+ gen（出生，同 genuine 真的）→ 生来如此、不加修饰
inhibit§Cold inhibits the reaction so completely that the same mixture is stable for years in a freezer.§低温如此彻底地**抑制**这个反应，同样的混合物在冷冻柜里能稳定多年。§in-（在内）+ hibit（拿住，同 prohibit 禁止）
inhibition§The drug's inhibition of one enzyme explains both its benefit and the four side effects that limit its use.§这种药对某种酶的**抑制**既解释了它的疗效，也解释了限制其使用的四种副作用。§
inhospitable§The climate is inhospitable for eight months, and the four thousand people here have arranged their whole year around that.§这里的气候八个月**不宜人居**，四千居民围绕这一点安排了全年。§
inimitable§Her inimitable style has been copied for forty years, always badly and always recognizably.§她**无法模仿的**风格被抄了四十年，每次都抄得很糟，每次都认得出来。§in-（不）+ imit（模仿，同 imitate 模仿）
initiate§She initiated the review that eventually named her own department, which is why people trusted it.§正是她**发起**了那场最终点到她自己部门的评审，所以人们信任它。§in-（进入）+ it（走，同 exit 出去）→ 迈出第一步
innocence§His innocence was established by a receipt that had been in the case file, unread, for nineteen years.§他的**清白**是靠一张在案卷里躺了十九年无人翻阅的收据确立的。§in-（不）+ noc（伤害，同 innocuous 无害的）
innocuous§The remark was innocuous in the room and looked very different in a headline the next morning.§这句话在当场是**无伤大雅的**，第二天早上出现在标题里就完全不同了。§in-（不）+ noc（伤害，同 noxious 有毒的）
innovation§The innovation was organizational, not technical: they simply stopped sending the form to four offices.§这项**创新**是组织性的而非技术性的——他们只是不再把表格送去四个办公室。§in-（进入）+ nov（新，同 novel 新奇的）
innovative§The most innovative feature is the one the marketing never mentioned, because nobody could explain it briefly.§最**有创意的**功能是营销从未提及的那个，因为没人能简短地解释它。§
innovator§The innovator died poor and the four companies that copied her design are still trading.§这位**创新者**去世时很穷，而抄袭她设计的四家公司至今仍在经营。§
inordinate§An inordinate share of the budget goes to compliance, and the compliance team has never once been audited.§预算中**过高的**一部分用于合规，而合规团队自己从未被审计过。§in-（不）+ ordin（秩序，同 order 顺序）→ 出了分寸
insatiable§His insatiable curiosity about other people's work made him the best reviewer the journal ever had.§他对别人工作**永不满足**的好奇心，让他成了这本期刊有过的最好的审稿人。§in-（不）+ sat（满足，同 satisfy 满足）
inscrutable§The decision remains inscrutable: the file contains four options and no record of why one was chosen.§这个决定至今**无从索解**——卷宗里有四个选项，却没有为何选中其一的记录。§in-（不）+ scrut（搜查，同 scrutiny 细查）→ 查不出所以然
insecurity§Job insecurity, not workload, is what the survey found people minded most about the new contracts.§调查发现人们最介意新合同的是工作的**不安全感**而非工作量。§
insensitive§The letter was insensitive rather than cruel, and the difference mattered to nobody who received it.§这封信是**不体察人情**而非残忍的，而这个区别对收信人来说毫无意义。§
inseparable§The two questions are inseparable in practice, and every attempt to answer one has raised the other.§这两个问题在实践中**不可分割**，每一次回答其一都会引出另一个。§
insidious§The damage is insidious: nothing visible for eleven years, and then a wall that cannot be saved.§这种损害是**潜伏渐进的**——十一年看不出任何迹象，然后是一面救不回来的墙。§in-（在内）+ sid（坐，同 reside 居住）→ 埋伏在里面
insightful§Her insightful comment reframed a debate that four earlier speakers had only made louder.§她**有洞察力的**评论重构了一场此前四位发言者只是把它吵得更响的辩论。§
insignificant§The difference is statistically insignificant and, for the four thousand people affected, entirely real.§这个差异在统计上**不显著**，而对受影响的四千人来说完全真实。§
insinuate§He insinuated that the funding had been arranged privately, and named nobody, and never repeated it.§他**含沙射影**地说经费是私下安排的，一个人名也没点，此后再没提过。§in-（进入）+ sinu（弯曲，同 sinuous 蜿蜒的）→ 拐着弯渗进去
insinuation§The insinuation did more harm than an open charge, because there was nothing specific to refute.§这种**暗讽**比公开指控伤害更大，因为没有具体的东西可以反驳。§
insipid§The wine was insipid and expensive, and the restaurant sold nine hundred bottles of it that year.§这款酒**寡淡**又昂贵，餐厅那年卖了九百瓶。§in-（不）+ sip（味道，同 savor 滋味）
insistence§Her insistence on seeing the raw data delayed publication by four months and saved the paper.§她**坚持**要看原始数据，让论文推迟四个月发表，也救了这篇论文。§
insistent§The noise was insistent rather than loud, and it took nine days to find where it came from.§这声音是**持续不断的**而非响亮的，花了九天才找到它从哪儿来。§
insolence§His insolence to the inspector was reported, and the inspection that followed found nine violations.§他对检查员的**傲慢无礼**被上报，随后的检查发现了九项违规。§in-（不）+ sol（习惯）→ 不按规矩来
insolent§The insolent reply was written at two in the morning and sent, unfortunately, at two in the morning.§这封**无礼的**回复写于凌晨两点，不幸的是也在凌晨两点发了出去。§
insolvent§The company was insolvent for nine months before anyone outside the finance office noticed.§这家公司**资不抵债**九个月，财务室以外才有人发觉。§in-（不）+ solv（解开／偿付，同 solve 解决）
instantaneous§The response was instantaneous and wrong, and the four seconds he did not take cost him the point.§反应是**瞬间的**而且是错的，他没花的那四秒让他输了这一分。§instant（即刻）
instigate§Nobody could prove who instigated the walkout, and forty people left the floor at the same minute.§没人能证明是谁**煽动**了这次罢工，四十个人在同一分钟离开了车间。§in-（进入）+ stig（刺，同 stimulate 刺激）
instinctive§Her instinctive reaction was to check the number again, and the number was indeed wrong.§她**本能的**反应是再核一遍数字，而这个数字确实错了。§in-（在内）+ stinct（刺，同 distinct 清晰的）
instructive§The failure was more instructive than the four successes, and the team wrote it up in detail.§这次失败比四次成功更**有教益**，团队把它详细写了下来。§
instructor§The instructor who taught him to read a chart in 1979 is the reason he survived the storm.§1979 年教他看图表的那位**教员**，是他挺过那场风暴的原因。§
